sequential_actual_reading_notes.note: Read both complete texts and matching displayed image. Exact v1 is 33 pages, submitted 6 October. Main Theorem1.3/6.1 is for a normal affine toric analytic pair with invariant rational D and K_X+D Q-Cartier; its sheaf is a coherent O-submodule of meromorphic functions, finitely generated by meromorphic monomials, not automatically an ordinary holomorphic ideal. Criterion shifts by rational u_D; cones may be non-full-dimensional. Weights subtracting rational monomial-ideal terms are separately scoped and generally non-psh. The norm-versus-squared-norm convention still needs the source definition.

Read complete source text and matching image. Corollary6.3 requires a nonzero coherent invariant ideal and positive rational c; its criterion tests every monomial generator after adding c a_j. Negative boundary coefficients lead to meromorphic fractional modules; effective D and locally upper-bounded weights are asserted to restore ordinary ideals. Coherence/strong openness and invariant-sheaf finite monomial generation are separate proof inputs. Toric spaces use saturated sigma-dual lattice semigroups and strong convexity, with no full-dimensional-cone restriction.

Read complete source text and displayed matching image. Orbit dimensions are r−dim sigma; X_sigma has one closed orbit even with a torus factor. The canonical divisor is minus the reduced toric boundary, and q(K+D)=div chi^(−q u_D), fixing the sign of the discrepancy shift. Psh on an analytic space is defined by a local ambient psh extension and excludes identically −infinity on a component; a singular-space extension assumption must remain explicit. Toric orbit/divisor and Cartier inputs are externally cited.

Read complete source text and displayed matching image. Disc criterion and removable singularity theorem retain local irreducibility and local upper bounds. The ideal weight is one-half log sum|f|² plus a locally bounded term; source I((X,D);phi) uses |f|² exp(−2phi) against an adapted pluricanonical volume on X_reg, so the book squared-norm weight must be 2phi. The sheaf initially lives in M_X and may have poles for negative D. Theorem3.2 equates analytic and analytified algebraic multiplier modules for a nonzero algebraic ideal with real c>0; its proof follows next. Source Definition3.1's target notation must be read with the preceding measurable extended-real convention.

Read the full texts and displayed image. Theorem3.2's log-resolution proof uses A=K_Y−q^−1 mu*(q(K_X+D)), phi_a∘mu=sum b_i log|z_i|+O(1), and an integral twist by ceil(a_i−c b_i). The residual exponents lie in (−1,0], so the weight is both integrable and locally bounded below; this yields the rounded divisor module after meromorphic L²-removability and proper pushforward. Proposition3.3 begins the effective-D no-pole proof at a generic smooth polar divisor, explicitly using normality and a locally upper-bounded weight.

Read complete texts and matching image. Effective-D no-pole divergence is completed with k≥1 and the weight's lower bound. Lemma3.4 computes the adapted pullback using integer qA, a holomorphic unit and the 2^n factor. Proposition3.5 twists by ceil A and adds the effective fractional divisor ceil A−A to the pulled-back weight; the alternative uses D_Y=−A. Properness supplies compact fibre coverage before shrinking a base neighbourhood, and meromorphic descent is invoked. These transformations are resolution-dependent descriptions with a quasi-psh weight, not a measurable-weight coherence theorem.

Read complete texts and matching displayed image. Lemma3.6 confirms the sign of the Cartier twist: I(D;phi)=h^−1 I(D+div h;phi), from dV_beta=|h|² dV_h^(−q)beta. Proposition3.7 clears denominators locally with a holomorphic h making D+div h effective. Corollary3.8 coherence uses quasi-psh pullback, smooth multiplier-ideal coherence and proper direct image. Strong openness retains fixed D, scales only phi, and compares (1+epsilon)phi_tilde_0≤phi_tilde_epsilon≤phi_tilde_0 after local constant normalization; compact fibre coverage must produce one positive epsilon in the continuation.

Read complete texts and matching image. Strong openness closes by finite compact-fibre cover, minimum epsilon and proper base shrinking. Remark3.10 distinguishes adapted-pair ideals from NO/GR measures and retains external attribution; its claimed local-complete-intersection coincidence is ancillary and not yet independently source-checked. Maximal non-lc ideals use effective D and perturb only discrepancies ≤−1, with changes at negative integers for epsilon<1/q; resolution independence and Proposition3.13 are imported from FST. Section4 introduces proper convex Legendre transforms and lower-semicontinuous recession functions; source sign/domain conventions remain to be checked against the integrability theorem.

Read complete texts and matching image, including the closure bars omitted by text extraction. Theorem4.3 sandwiches dom(g+delta_{−sigma})* between dom g*+sigma-dual and its closure. Lemma4.4 identifies the closed domain via non-strict recession inequalities and its ambient interior via strict inequalities for every nonzero cone direction. Theorem4.6 is stated only for a full-dimensional closed cone and a finite convex g, with exp(2(<m,x>−g(x))) integrability. Extending its Lebesgue integral to a lower-dimensional cone would be invalid; the later main proof must use full-dimensional resolution charts.

Read complete texts and matching image. Theorem4.6 sufficiency uses strictly positive recession and linear coercivity; necessity uses a positive-volume half-tube and concavity, not just a measure-zero ray. Remark4.7 obtains uniform decay for compact transverse parameters by adding their compact convex-hull indicator. Lemma5.1 derives sigma-direction monotonicity from compact monomial-coordinate polydisks, upper bounds and one-variable convexity; the finite convex torus profile and normal removable-extension converse remain in scope. The coercivity theorem is a load-bearing external locator to check.

Read complete source text and matching image. Lemma5.1 converse uses finite convex continuity, an affine-envelope representation, Minkowski–Weyl decomposition S_R=P_R−sigma and normal removable extension, retaining local upper bounds. Newton body is dom(g+delta_{−sigma})*, not necessarily closed; actual image confirms closure bar in Proposition5.3. Proposition5.4's exact intersection argument over a finite smooth subdivision retains full-dimensional sigma and matches An's chart definition. Saturated N_sigma admits a splitting N=N_sigma⊕N', giving a torus factor and closed orbit {z0}×T_N', rather than a fixed point in the whole space.

Read the entire source text and matching image. Theorem5.5 globalizes monomial stalk generation at a point of the closed orbit by coherence, invariant translates and orbit-closure intersection. Lemma5.6 averages global Stein sections, not stalks at a potentially moving point. Fourier projections land in the ideal via a continuous coherent quotient; their nonzero weights are scalar characters. The finite-jet functions F_l(k) have all Fourier coefficients zero, giving f_z∈J+m_z^l for every l, then Krull intersection gives f_z∈J. No assumption that the chosen closed-orbit point is fixed is used in this jet argument. Finite generation follows from Noetherianity in the continuation.

Read complete texts and matching image. Noetherianity closes Lemma5.6. Corollary5.8 clears denominators using the coherent invariant colon ideal (O:F), represented locally as a kernel into (O/hO)^l, then chooses one monomial denominator and applies ideal monomial generation. Theorem5.9 upgrades K_N invariance by holomorphic one-parameter subgroup maps into coherent quotient section spaces; the scalar identity theorem and continuous dual separate points. Local equality is extended along compact orbit paths, and fractional modules are reduced by the invariant denominator ideal. Fourier averaging and one-parameter continuation are distinct steps; zero-module case is trivial.

Read complete texts and matching image. Proposition5.10 reduces non-psh phi−c phi_a to a finite intersection for pairs (X,D−c div chi^{a_j}), using comparability of a positive power of a finite sum to the sum of those powers. Rational c preserves Q-Cartierness; strong openness scales only phi with c and ideal fixed. Theorem6.1 handles sigma=0 separately, then clears a monomial denominator and reduces to one closed-orbit stalk. It splits cone and torus directions and chooses compact annular transverse parameters. The proposed replacement of a monomial polydisk log region by translated cone tails requires a cofinal-neighbourhood interpretation, to check in the continuation.

Read complete source text and matching image. Main proof's adapted torus measure gives exp(2(<m+u_D,Log t>−g)) with angular constant (4pi)^r; torus-factor coefficients stay bounded on compact annuli, and Fubini plus uniform transverse coercivity supply necessity/sufficiency. Literal Log(U∩T)= (−sigma−b)×Omega' cannot be an exact equality with U open and a closed cone tail; it must be expressed using cofinal neighbourhood inclusions (and harmless boundaries), not copied as an equality. Example6.2 retains the even-sum character lattice of the A1 cone and u_D=(1/2,1); predicted ideals (z1,z3,z2²) versus (z1,z2,z3) need exact semigroup diagnostics. Corollary6.3 confirms the +c a_j shift. Remark6.4 broadens quasi-psh to a locally bounded measurable perturbation, distinct from Section3's conventional smooth-remainder terminology.

Read complete source text and displayed image. Locally bounded measurable perturbations preserve both multiplier modules and Newton domains on the compact closure of Log^{-1}(−sigma); this is broader than the earlier conventional quasi-psh definition and should be described explicitly. Corollary6.5 recovers lc reduced toric boundary and klt Q-Gorenstein toric spaces, retaining effective-D ordinary-ideal scope and the externally cited maximal non-lc identification. References1–23 include An thesis, Blickle, Cox–Little–Schenck, adapted EGZ volume, resolution, strong openness, Guenancia and FST; they are now read as bibliography metadata, not counted as dependency proof reading.

Read the complete final source text and displayed matching image. References24–34 identify Zhenqian Li's distinct multiplier-ideal variants and Kollár question, Nadel, Narasimhan, Oda, Rashkovskii, Rockafellar and Rockafellar–Wets. The 33-page controlling v1 has now been read completely in 17 displayed sheets with sequential notes. Prop.1.9 on p.5 and full proof p.6 characterize exponential integrability by ordinary interior, not closed-body boundary membership. Necessity uses Fubini on a positive-volume family of rays, differentiability almost everywhere, monotone directional derivative, and a separating nonnegative vector. The logarithmic change t=-log r has lower endpoint -log(radius), although the text prints log(radius); restricting to radius 1 removes that harmless local normalization typo.
